source.title: Mechanistic Tomography: Designed Measurement for Control-Oriented Interpretability

record.tranche_reason: Tests conditional effects of attention-head-group ablations on an IOI output margin and on held-out subset interventions. This is a conceptual test of self-repair and attribution consequences, rather than the original layer-level measurement.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the GPT-2-small IOI group-ablation interactions and held-out prediction of head-group subset interventions. Other experiments on HMMs, Tracr, and Qwen measure different subjects or intervention questions and are not rows for these claim versions. The paper cites earlier self-repair work, but cited results are not recorded.
record.test_reason: On GPT-2-small IOI, the study ablates documented head groups (Primary, Backup and Negative Name Movers) alone and together. It measures the nonadditive interaction in the IO−S logit margin under template-conditioned mean and zero ablation. Positive P×B and P×E interactions directly show backup-head compensation and conditional copy suppression after primary heads are removed. This is a different method aimed at the same self-repair question, on one narrow task and model.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Complete group ablations on GPT-2-small IOI reproduce conditional backup (P×B) and show a larger conditional copy-suppression interaction (P×E). The ordering P×E > P×B > B×E holds across all eight prompt conditions and both ablation conventions. In held-out subset prediction P×E gives the largest, most stable gain, while P×B's gain is small. The authors stress that the pair terms are group-level, leave a three-way residual, and the predictive comparison uses one template and mean ablation.
record.recipe_differences: The paper measures IOI head-group interactions and held-out predictions of subset interventions using an IOI logit margin. It does not reproduce layer ablation or full-distribution single-head ablation measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Direct interaction magnitudes differ between template-conditioned mean and zero ablation. Predictive comparison is limited to one prompt template and mean ablation; the tested group-pair terms have different predictive value.

fits_no_version.finding: Backup and Negative Name Mover groups interact positively under complete ablation (0.502 mean, 0.518 zero). The B×E term adds no held-out predictive value.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-primary head groups in a circuit interact nonadditively even without a compensation interpretation.

record.problems: For the self-repair-related evidence, the pretrained-model test is one model and a narrow IOI setting. Predictive subset comparison uses one prompt template and mean ablation. Effects are measured at the documented head-group level, not for individual head pairs; the study reports a remaining three-way residual.
record.rows_left_out: No additional numeric IOI group-interaction or held-out prediction results relevant to V5–V7 were left out. The paper states that the interaction ordering holds in every tested lexical/order condition but does not give separate numeric interaction values for each condition, so no per-condition numeric rows could be extracted.

untested.parts: No whole-layer attention ablation and no measurement of compensation by later layers.
No late-MLP erasure or downregulation measurements.
Groups of heads on the narrow IOI task only. No single-head ablations on general text, and no other model families or sizes.
No per-prompt variability of compensation, no fraction-restored measure, and no overcorrection test.
Final LayerNorm rescaling and anti-erasure neurons not tested. The fraction of self-repair these groups carry is not quantified, and the analysis is group-level, not individual heads.
Resample ablation not tested; only template-conditioned mean versus zero ablation on IOI.
No general evaluation of ablation-based importance scores across tasks or models. Predictive comparison uses one template and mean ablation only.

missing.what: Three-way residual after pairwise terms in the direct group study: 0.319 [0.215, 0.439] under mean ablation, 0.601 [0.417, 0.790] under zero ablation. Currently buried in r16's note.
Per-pair normalized interactions: P×E is 6.8× (mean) and 5.3× (zero) the P×B effect. The P×E − P×B contrast is 0.750 [0.562, 0.934] (mean) and 0.413 [0.207, 0.611] (zero).
Per-head additive baseline (MAE 0.379, R² 0.759). Fold-assignment stability: P×B gain positive in 199/200 assignments, P×E in 200/200.

record.verdict_notes: The self-repair evidence is confined to the IOI section of a broader methods paper. The HMM, Tracr and Qwen experiments do not bear on any version. The held-out prediction rows compare the study's own observer families and bear only indirectly on V7. The illustrative 1.5-logit margin flip example is hypothetical and should not be a row.

versions.untested_parts: No layer-level attention ablation with later attention layers measured for compensation.
No late-MLP downregulation or earlier-component ablation test.
The IOI experiment uses groups of heads on a narrow task, not single-head ablations on general text across model families and sizes.
The study does not quantify prompt-level variability in compensation or test overcorrection beyond the original effect.

Tests group-level conditional backup and copy-suppression effects on IOI; does not test final LayerNorm rescaling or anti-erasure neurons, identify every individual head-pair mechanism, or establish what fraction of self-repair is carried by these parts.
Compares template-conditioned mean and zero ablation for three IOI head-group interactions; does not test resample ablation or other tasks and models.
Tests additive group-effect prediction against group interactions on IOI, not the accuracy of general ablation-based importance scores across models or tasks.

rows.operation_detail: Ablated the Primary Name Mover (P) and Backup Name Mover (B) head groups and measured their interaction in the IO-versus-subject margin.

rows.measure: I_PB = Δ(P+B) − Δ(P) − Δ(B), in logits
rows.note: Positive interaction means joint removal causes more margin damage than the separate effects predict, consistent with conditional backup. Aggregate across the stated prompt conditions.

rows.subject: GPT-2-small
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the Negative Name Mover (E) group and measured its effect on the IO-versus-subject margin.
rows.measure: Δ(E), clean margin minus ablated margin, in logits
rows.note: Removing E alone improves the IO-versus-subject margin on this task.
rows.check: State 'reversed' is misleading. A negative Δ(E) is the expected sign for copy-suppression heads, not the opposite of any version. It is a component of the P×E interaction, read together with r9.

rows.subject: GPT-2-small
rows.operation_detail: Ablated P and E together and measured their joint effect on the IO-versus-subject margin.
rows.measure: Δ(P+E), clean margin minus ablated margin, in logits
rows.note: The joint ablation gives only a small margin improvement compared with removing E alone.
rows.check: State 'reversed' is wrong. Once P is removed, E's removal gives almost no boost (−0.136 vs −2.270 alone). This matches conditional copy suppression (E backs off when the primary signal is gone), which is what V5 names.

source_check.problem: The value is the joint effect relative to clean; the verdict-fix gloss incorrectly treats it as E's incremental effect after removing P.

relation.reason: Own IOI experiments measure conditional backup, conditional copy suppression, and failures of additive intervention prediction.

tranche.reason: Group co-ablation interactions and held-out subset prediction test compensation and its attribution consequences using a different method.

source_check.notes: All listed numeric values and intervals match. The authors-conclusion paraphrase is supported; interaction terms are group-level and incomplete, with unquantified repair shares. Cross-study counts, exclusivity, and author-overlap claims were not independently verifiable from this study.

statements.correction: Δ(E): −2.270 mean, −2.335 zero. Δ(P+E), relative to clean: −0.136 mean, −0.769 zero. Conditional E effect after P removal: Δ(P+E) − Δ(P). I_PE: 1.830 mean, 1.681 zero.
statements.problem: The wording presents joint P+E effects as though they were E's conditional effects after P removal.

statements.correction: P×B MAE improvement: 0.0083. P×E MAE improvement on the same subset distribution: 0.1265. Section 5.5 distinguishes corner interactions from average predictive contributions; it does not establish an exclusive corner condition for attribution error.
statements.problem: The small incremental P×B gain does not establish that additive scores generally misstate little or that substantial errors occur only near full removal.

statements.correction: Original-template single-group effects: P 0.463, B 0.350. Joint effect: 1.869. Demonstrated discrepancy: nonadditivity and conditional effects, not an incorrect P-versus-B ordering.
statements.problem: P > B is correctly reported, but this study does not establish that this ordering itself is a misranking.

statements.correction: Small average predictive contribution applies to P×B. P×E improves MAE by 0.1265 over the same masks. Δ(P+E) = −0.136 relative to clean; E's conditional effect is Δ(P+E) − Δ(P).
statements.problem: The corner-only qualification overgeneralizes the small P×B gain; −0.136 is also a joint effect rather than E's conditional effect.

statements.correction: E-alone effects: −2.270 mean, −2.335 zero. Joint P+E effects relative to clean: −0.136 mean, −0.769 zero. Conditional E effects require subtracting Δ(P). The MAE 0.259 predictor adds P×E.
statements.problem: The phrase describing E with P also ablated conflates joint and conditional effects.
